mainEntity.name: Can functional medicine help IBS and leaky gut?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We treat digestive symptoms by addressing what is driving them, the microbiome, the gut lining, and inflammation, rather than only muting them. Most people see bloating, regularity, and energy improve as the root causes are corrected.

mainEntity.name: How is a functional gut workup different from my GI doctor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your GI doctor rules out structural disease, and that matters. As a functional medicine gut health doctor in Atlanta, Dr. Nina Ross maps the whole digestive and immune picture and builds a personalized plan, testing, nutrition, and targeted repair, to address the cause.

mainEntity.name: What testing do you run for gut issues?

acceptedAnswer.text: We go beyond a normal scope, with comprehensive stool and microbiome testing, food-reaction panels, inflammation markers, and nutrient status, so the plan targets your specific root causes.

mainEntity.name: Do I have to give up gluten and dairy forever?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. We use testing and a structured reintroduction to find your true triggers, so you end up with the widest, most comfortable diet your gut can handle, not a permanent list of fears.

mainEntity.name: Is bloating really something you can fix?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes. Bloating usually points to the microbiome, digestion, or an inflamed gut. When we address the cause, most people notice flatter, calmer days within weeks.

mainEntity.name: Can my gut be behind my fatigue and mood?

acceptedAnswer.text: Frequently. The gut is in constant conversation with your brain and immune system. Calm the gut at the root and energy, focus, and mood often lift alongside digestion.

mainEntity.name: Do you offer virtual gut care or only in person in Atlanta?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both. See Dr. Nina Ross in person at our Atlanta clinic, or virtually anywhere in Georgia. Your $99 Symptom Consultation can be booked either way.

sections.label: Hero

headings.text: Root-cause gut and digestion care in Atlanta that finally settles your stomach.

paragraphs: If the bloating, the reflux, the unpredictable bathroom trips and the food list that keeps shrinking have become your normal, you are not imagining it.

Your gut has been trying to tell you something, and it deserves someone who will listen to the whole story. At Nina Ross Functional Medicine, we treat digestion at its root, here in Atlanta and virtually across Georgia. Dr. Nina Ross follows the whole picture, the microbiome, the gut lining, and the foods that inflame you, until she finds what is really driving your symptoms, then builds the plan around your body and your life.

sections.label: Why conventional care misses it

headings.text: You were handed an antacid and a shrug.

eyebrowSpans: Why conventional care keeps missing it
paragraphs: A fifteen-minute visit rarely has room to look at the whole digestive system. So gut symptoms get silenced one at a time, and the thing connecting them goes unexamined.

boldPairs.title: What you’re usually told
boldPairs.body: “Your scope looked fine. It is probably just IBS, try to manage the stress.”

boldPairs.title: What’s actually happening
boldPairs.body: The microbiome, the gut lining, and inflammation are feeding each other in a loop. Calm the loop and digestion settles together.

sections.label: The functional medicine difference

headings.text: We will not silence your gut and call it healed.

paragraphs: Here is where we part ways with conventional care. The reflex answer for a struggling gut is a pill that turns down the signal, an antacid, a laxative, something to mute it. That can quiet the surface for a while. But muting a symptom does not heal a gut. The moment you stop, it returns, and the root cause has had more time to dig in.
We would rather do the harder, more honest work. We find what is actually irritating your gut and we treat that.
If a medication still has a place in your care, that should be your informed choice, made with the full picture in front of you, not a default handed to you in a fifteen minute visit.

boldPairs.title: It mutes the signal, not the cause
boldPairs.body: An antacid lowers the acid, it does not answer why your gut is inflamed in the first place.

boldPairs.title: It can starve your microbiome
boldPairs.body: Long-term acid blockers and repeated antibiotics can thin the very ecosystem digestion depends on.

boldPairs.title: It postpones the real repair
boldPairs.body: A gut left inflamed keeps leaking, and the food reactions and fatigue tend to widen over time.

sections.label: The root-cause view

headings.text: Gut trouble runs in a loop. We map the whole circle.

paragraphs: Each driver pushes the next. That is why treating one in isolation rarely holds, and why mapping the full cycle changes everything.
When we investigate your gut, we read the whole digestive and immune picture rather than a single scope, and connect each driver back to what you’re feeling:

strongBullets.full: Microbiome imbalance, the bloating, the gas, and the cravings that seem to run the show.

strongBullets.label: A leaky gut lining
strongBullets.full: A leaky gut lining, where food particles slip through and the immune system starts reacting.

strongBullets.label: Chronic inflammation
strongBullets.full: Chronic inflammation, the quiet thread linking your gut to your joints, skin, and mood.

strongBullets.label: Food sensitivities
strongBullets.full: Food sensitivities, the meals that should be fine but leave you bloated and foggy.

strongBullets.label: Low stomach acid & enzymes
strongBullets.full: Low stomach acid & enzymes, behind the reflux, the heaviness, and feeling full too fast.

strongBullets.label: Cortisol & stress
strongBullets.full: Cortisol & stress, tightens digestion and keeps the gut on high alert.

strongBullets.label: The gut-brain axis
strongBullets.full: The gut-brain axis, where poor digestion quietly turns into low mood and brain fog.
